title: A SIGTERM or SIGHUP that reaches runner start before its child runs writes no status, so the manager gets no signal and a previous run's status stays
goal: autopilot.runner_start writes a status with cause error (naming the signal) when RunnerEnded is raised before the run's own status is kept (during prepare_worktree or register_runner), exactly as a signal during the run does; a planted-failure test raises RunnerEnded at each of those points and reads the status; found by the SP-itmjxudu review

run: import sys,pathlib,tempfile;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import autopilot;r=pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp());autopilot.register_runner=lambda root,sprint:(_ for _ in ()).throw(autopilot.RunnerEnded("SIGTERM"));autopilot.runner_start("SP-aaaaaaaa",root=r);sys.exit(0 if list(r.rglob("status.json")) else 1)
